title: Preservation of Scripture
definition: The Preservation of Scripture means God has faithfully kept His Word available to His people so that His truth is not lost.
summary: The Preservation of Scripture means God has faithfully kept His Word available to His people so that His truth is not lost.
christFocus: Jesus taught that God’s Word will not pass away, and His saving work is proclaimed through the preserved witness of Scripture.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God’s Word has endured because God is faithful. Across generations, opposition, persecution, copying, translation, and human weakness, the Lord has preserved His truth so His people may continue to hear His voice.

Preservation does not mean every printed copy, translation, or teacher is perfect. It means God has not allowed His Word to disappear from His Church. Believers can have confidence that Scripture still faithfully reveals God, Christ, salvation, and the way of discipleship.

The preserved Word keeps pointing people to the living Christ. The same Gospel preached by the apostles remains the message sinners need today: Christ died, Christ rose, Christ reigns, and Christ saves.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
A person may wonder whether the Bible can still be trusted after so many centuries. Preservation answers that fear with God’s own faithfulness. The Lord who gives His Word also keeps His Word.

This matters especially for ministry beyond comfort and convenience. If Iron Sharpener is used offline, in recovery spaces, in hardship, or by people without access to constant internet, the preserved Word remains enough to feed faith.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Thank God for preserving His Word and treat Scripture as a treasure, not a disposable resource. Read it, teach it carefully, share it freely, and trust that the God who kept His Word through generations can use it powerfully in your life today.
